response.text:
Weak Electronics history sensitivity is consistent with popularity shortcuts, but does not establish their cause. A [2024 sequential-recommendation study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) compared random, popularity, in-batch, mixed and adaptive negatives: random sampling reinforced head-item bias; popularity-based sampling improved balance across popularity bands, sometimes reducing aggregate accuracy. Thus, changing the sampler can change both learning difficulty and popularity bias without changing SASRec’s representation. Hard negatives also risk penalizing plausible unobserved positives; the [negative-sampling survey](https://doi.org/10.1145/3793855) identifies false negatives and optimization instability as persistent concerns.

Scalable objective alternatives include full-catalog cross-entropy as a reference and [Scalable Cross-Entropy (RecSys 2024)](https://dspace.mit.edu/entities/publication/5392aca9-0bae-4176-9b3a-a8165957ba26), which uses maximum-inner-product search to approximate softmax over informative catalog subsets, reporting up to 100× lower peak memory in its experiments. [Correcting the LogQ Correction (RecSys 2025)](https://github.com/NonameUntitled/logq/) supplies SASRec implementations covering full softmax, uniform/in-batch/mixed sampled softmax, and original versus revised sampling corrections—useful for controlled comparisons.

Suggested experiment, rather than an established literature conclusion: freeze architecture, preprocessing and seeds; compare BCE, full softmax where feasible, uniform sampled softmax, and mixed sampling with appropriate correction, recording negative count and GPU cost. Add moderate hard-negative mining only afterward, excluding known training positives. Measure validation degradation after history replacement, truncation and order shuffling; report popularity-band results alongside each category’s HR@10 and the four-category macro average. Compare equal compute and learning curves to distinguish insufficient optimization from objective effects. These diagnostics can identify history dependence; they cannot prove unobserved user preferences or guarantee gains under the pinned evaluator.
